text:
maya: Heads-up — in the last hour we saw a spike of 413s on /v1/embeddings for a handful of mid-market tenants. SLA alerts fired for two customers. stack traces point to the splitter rejecting payloads instead of falling back.

maya: example log: `request_id=rid_4a3 size_bytes=6.2MB dims=1024` -> `413 Payload Too Large` from embed-splitter

tom: ugh. Is this the old hard-fail behavior or a new preflight change?

jeremy: it's the hard-fail path. splitter currently enforces both per-vector dims and total-bytes limits and returns 413. There's an opt-in flag `oversize_tolerance` in runtime that can accept and truncate/partial-success but it's disabled by default.

sara: where are we on telemetry for this? we need counters to triage — reject_count, truncate_count, per-tenant sample blobs, and a histogram for bytes. Also a dashboard tile in Console (per-route oversize heatmap).

alex: big API semantics question: do we want to return partial successes (per-item status) or keep the all-or-nothing 413? returning mixed success affects SDKs and billing.

maya: product asked for graceful behavior for embeddings ingestion — prefer partial succeeds + per-item status so customers can retry only failures. they also want clear billing semantics.

tom: billing-wise I'd charge only for items that actually produced embeddings. But we need to clearly document it. Also p95 latency could jump if we do truncation/extra parsing.

jeremy: sample response proposal (inline):
```
HTTP 200
{
  "request_id":"rid_4a3",
  "results":[
    {"index":0, "status":"ok", "embedding": [0.1,...]},
    {"index":1, "status":"rejected", "reason":"dims_mismatch"}
  ]
}
```
This keeps a single HTTP 200 but has per-item states.

sara: +1 for metrics. we should emit `embed.item_rejected{reason=...,tenant=...}` and sample the original payload hash for debugging (never store raw text). Also add a trace tag so Console can link to logs.

alex: alternative is HTTP 207 Multi-Status but that confuses clients. I prefer 200 with explicit statuses. less surprising than 413 which wipes everything.

maya: runtime concern: if we enable oversize_tolerance it can increase memory pressure because we attempt to process larger requests. we need an autoscaling/circuit for the dedicated pools.

jeremy: agree. rollout plan idea: 1) add telemetry + dashboard 2) add opt-in feature flag in tenant config 3) run canary on 5 tenants with `oversize_tolerance=true` (low qps) 4) monitor `reject_rate`, `truncate_rate`, p95 latency and GPU memory alloc trends 5) then broaden.

tom: add alerting rules: reject_rate > 1% sustained for 15m -> page eng-sre. p95 latency blowup > 2x -> page.

sara: Console UX: create a per-tenant card: "Oversize events" with sample hashes, last 10 rejects, and a toggle to opt-in (with warning) + link to RFC. Also a heatmap under route metrics.

alex: dev-experience: SDKs should expose `per_item_status` in responses and provide a helper `retry_failed(items)` util. we'll need to coordinate release notes.

maya: about billing: confirm with finance, but we should bill for successful item tokens only. we'll need a webhook to emit an "embed.billing_event" for each success to downstream billing.

jeremy: I'll sketch an RFC and include the sample response format, metric names (`embed.reject_count`, `embed.truncate_count`, `embed.item_ok_count`), rollout steps, and autoscaler knobs.

maya: action items: jeremy -> RFC by EOD tomorrow; sara -> telemetry + console mockups by Friday; alex -> SDK contract doc; tom -> define alert thresholds; infra-bot -> add canary flag gating.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Flag `oversize_tolerance` created in config-service (default=false). Canary toggle ready under `/feature-flags`.

maya: thanks all. we'll reconvene after RFC. :thumbsup:
